page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.6xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache. Supported instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES-NI, and BMI2.

The system is provisioned with 96.0 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. For network connectivity, the instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs included on this instance type.

Benchmark data illustrates typical general-purpose behavior for its processor generation. While single-thread throughput is modest, scoring in lower percentiles in Geekbench single-core (1008.0) and stress-ng single-core (1107.98), multi-threaded scaling reaches the middle tier. PassMark CPU reaches 18227.84, Geekbench multi-core registers 7786.0, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression hits 76.24 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth reaches 90.15 GB/sec on large 256 MB blocks, supporting Redis throughput of 16.81 million SET operations per second and static web throughput of 13.07 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g5.6xlarge provides balanced compute and memory capacity for enterprise workloads that do not demand cutting-edge single-core IPC. Because local disk storage is absent, storage costs scale separately via external block storage. The configuration is functionally appropriate for general web serving, software compilation, multi-threaded enterprise application runtimes, caching layers, and relational or document database engines.
